questions.cardText:
[Economics] What is “Pareto Efficiency”?
A. The maximum rate of production
B. A situation where no one can be better off without making another worse off
C. The optimal allocation of resources under government intervention
Answer: B. In perfectly competitive markets, if certain conditions are met (e.g., perfect information), the market equilibrium is Pareto Efficient, meaning resources are allocated in the most efficient way possible.
questions.de: Wie heißt in der Ökonomie ein Zustand, in dem niemand bessergestellt werden kann, ohne einen anderen schlechterzustellen?
questions.en: What is the economic term for a situation in which no one can be made better off without making someone else worse off?

timeline.labelEn: Vilfredo Pareto, Italian economist after whom Pareto efficiency is named
timeline.labelDe: Vilfredo Pareto, italienischer Ökonom, nach dem die Pareto-Effizienz benannt ist

questions.notes: Also called Pareto optimality. Question and answer swapped so the open question has a short answer.

questions.cardText:
[Art History] What does the “Renaissance” art movement primarily focus on?
A. Abstract forms
B. Humanism and realism
C. Surrealism
Answer: B.
questions.de: Auf welche Geisteshaltung konzentrierte sich die Kunst der Renaissance neben dem Realismus vor allem?
questions.en: Besides realism, which philosophy did Renaissance art primarily focus on?
questions.notes: Wikipedia: Renaissance art spread together with Renaissance humanist philosophy, with naturalism/realism and close observation of the human figure. Dates 1350–1620 as given in the article (approximate).
